items.title: Scandic’s Dalata Deal Just Got Its First Report Card
items.summary: Scandic paid €500 million for a business that fills more rooms and earns more per room than its own operation. The first combined numbers back the deal. The test now is whether it can integrate slowly enough to protect the occupancy that made Dalata worth buying.

items.title: Playing Catch-Up: Can American Close the Gap With Delta and United?
items.summary: American is the biggest U.S. airline but the least profitable of the Big Three. The changes underway are widespread: from new routes and premium offerings to Tate’s cookies.

items.title: Delhi’s Smog Collides With India’s Peak Tourism Season
items.summary: Air quality in northern India has plummeted as the so-called pollution season gets underway. It is now a regular feature of traveling to the region in winter. Masks have emerged as a solution — a Band-Aid to a structural problem fueled by emissions.

items.title: Visit Oslo Follows Its Viral Anti-Ad With a Horror Christmas Musical
items.summary: Visit Oslo needed a unique twist to its "Is It Even a City?" sequel to help fill hotels in the winter. Its project manager says the final result is almost as popular as the original.

items.title: What Happens When the Destination Comes Second?
items.summary: Tourism marketing has to account for travelers whose plans begin with an experience rather than a place.

items.title: Duffel-Katanox Partnership Targets AI Agents, Hotel Booking Breakdowns
items.summary: For travel sellers building AI agents, booking the room is only part of the job. Duffel and Katanox want to bring payments, commissions, and financing into the same system.

items.title: Malaysia Airlines Overtakes AirAsia on India Routes by Standing Still
items.summary: AirAsia’s fuel-driven retreat should be a gift to its rivals, but high fuel costs and scarce aircraft mean few can afford to take advantage. Malaysia Airlines has overtaken it on India routes with 1% more seats in a market that shrank 10%. The longer AirAsia stays small, the more

items.title: Ras Al Khaimah Airport Courts Wynn’s Jet Set but Waits on Airlines
items.summary: Ras Al Khaimah’s airport is betting on Wynn’s new integrated resort and other luxury hotels to bring in five-star travelers. For now, it is upgrading the terminal it has and holding the new one until airlines commit. The resort’s delay pushes any payoff to late 2027.
